full_text_en:
Hainan Nanyang Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Hainan Success Investment Co., Ltd.

v.

Nanyang Shipping Group Co., Ltd., Chen Lin, and Hainan Jincan Commercial Trade Co., Ltd.

— Action for Third-Party Revocation

Ruling Summary

The institutional function of an action for third-party revocation is to provide relief to a person not party to the proceedings who, for reasons not attributable to such person, failed to participate in the proceedings, and where the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement is erroneous and impairs such person’s civil rights and interests. In practice, it is necessary both to protect the legitimate rights of persons not party to the proceedings in accordance with the law and to prevent abuse of the action for third-party revocation from undermining the stability of effective judgments. Where a person not party to the proceedings who brings a revocation action cannot fully prove that the effective judgment, ruling, or mediation agreement is indeed erroneous and impairs such person’s civil rights and interests, the claim shall be dismissed.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Supreme People’s Court Civil Final No. 712

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Hainan Nanyang Real Estate Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 701, Unit 1, Xinghai Jiayuan, West Side of Erhuan South Road, Dongfang City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Li Guojun, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Xue Weifang, lawyer of Hainan Haixin Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Pu, lawyer of Beijing Joy & Glory Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Hainan Success Investment Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room 108, Building 8, Yongnanyuan Residential Community, Nanhai Avenue, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Cheng Yong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Zhenyu, lawyer of Beijing Dentons Law Offices, LLP.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Chen Lin, male, born March 13, 1966, Han Chinese, domiciled at Wuchang District, Wuhan City, Hubei Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Rongyou, lawyer of Hubei Fahui Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Nanyang Shipping Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Rooms 2006 and 2007, Nanyang Mansion, No. 81 Binhai Avenue, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Jing, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Xie Xin, lawyer of Beijing Dentons Law Offices, LLP.

Appellee (Third Party at First Instance): Hainan Jincan Commercial Trade Co., Ltd. Domicile: West Side of Erhuan Road, Basuo Town, Dongfang City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Chen Lin, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Rongyou, lawyer of Hubei Fahui Law Firm.

In the case of action for third-party revocation brought by appellants Hainan Nanyang Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nanyang Real Estate Company) and Hainan Success Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hainan Success Company) against appellees Nanyang Shipping Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nanyang Shipping Company), Chen Lin, and Hainan Jincan Commercial Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hainan Jincan Company), the appellants, dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2018) E Min Chu No. 77 rendered by the Hubei High People’s Court, appealed to this Court. This Court, after filing the case on April 29, 2019, formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. Xue Weifang and Wang Pu, agents ad litem of appellant Nanyang Real Estate Company, Li Zhenyu, agent ad litem of appellant Hainan Success Company, Xie Xin, agent ad litem of appellee Nanyang Shipping Company, and Zhang Rongyou, the jointly appointed agent ad litem of appellees Chen Lin and Hainan Jincan Company, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

Appellant Nanyang Real Estate Company’s appeal requests: 1. To set aside the judgment of first instance and amend it to uphold all of its claims; 2. To have Chen Lin bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Facts and reasons: 1. The judgment of first instance was erroneous in finding that Nanyang Real Estate Company does not enjoy the right to use the land in dispute. (a) The land in dispute was lawfully approved and acquired by Nanyang Real Estate Company. Although Nanyang Real Estate Company did not obtain the state-owned land use right certificate, the relevant approval documents for the land transfer, the state-owned land use right transfer contract, and the land acquisition agreement were all handled and signed in the name of Nanyang Real Estate Company. Under the premise that neither Nanyang Real Estate Company nor Nanyang Shipping Company holds the state-owned land use right certificate for the land in dispute, the approval subject of other administrative documents and the subject making investments should serve as the basis for determining the owner of the land use right. The court of first instance should not have used the failure to obtain the state-owned land use right certificate as a reason to exclude Nanyang Real Estate Company’s legitimate rights and interests in the land in dispute. (b) The court of first instance erroneously severed the relationship between the land in dispute and other parcels of land in the project to which it belongs. Nanyang Real Estate Company has paid all but RMB 328,000 of the outstanding balance of the state-owned land use right transfer fee and land acquisition fee for the land in dispute, and has made substantial investments in the surrounding infrastructure of the land in dispute. Based on Nanyang Real Estate Company’s relevant investments, the land in dispute should be found to belong to Nanyang Real Estate Company. (c) The land in dispute is part of the land acquired under the Land Acquisition (Allocation) Agreement dated June 24, 1995, and was acquired and invested in by Nanyang Real Estate Company. (d) The Dongfang City People’s Government and the Bureau of Land and Resources of Hainan Province did not provide any cadastral records showing that the transferee under Approval No. (1994) 26 and the state-owned land use right transfer contract was changed from Nanyang Real Estate Company to Nanyang Shipping Company, nor did they state that the merger of legal personality of Nanyang Shipping Company and Nanyang Real Estate Company caused the land use right to change hands. Their sole basis was the Civil Mediation Agreement (2003) Wu Qu Min Chu Zi No. 265 of the Wuchang District People’s Court of Wuhan City, Hubei Province. This indicates that the Dongfang City Bureau of Land and Resources and the People’s Government of Hainan Province did not make an independent determination on the ownership of the land in dispute, and their defense submissions cannot be cited by the court of first instance and used as the basis for confirming the rights to the land in dispute. (e) The historical evolution of Nanyang Real Estate Company did not cause it to lose its rights to the project land in the Basuo Development Zone and even to the land in dispute. The restructuring documents of Nanyang Shipping Company contain descriptions of Nanyang Shipping Company’s assets. The financial statements and audit reports can accurately and truthfully reflect the objective situation of Nanyang Shipping Company’s assets and can prove that the land in dispute was not recorded within the asset scope of Nanyang Shipping Company. Nanyang Real Estate Company once lost its independent legal personality and later restored it. During the above process, Nanyang Real Estate Company’s rights to the project land, including the land in dispute, were not affected. 2. The judgment of first instance was erroneous in finding that the loan of RMB 2 million was genuine. The loan of RMB 2 million was not actually made, and the court of first instance failed to perform a reasonable duty of review. The allocation of the burden of proof was unreasonable. Chen Lin was unable to provide any evidence of the actual occurrence of the large loan of RMB 2 million. In the investigation of the criminal case, he twice told the public security authorities that RMB 1.3 million was a commission he asked Fan Yunhai to collect for him from Chen Weiqing, and that Fan Yunhai signed the IOU as a promise to collect it for him, rather than being an actual loan paid to Hainan Success Company. After Fan Yunhai’s death, Chen Lin and Nanyang Shipping Company signed the Repayment Guarantee Agreement, stipulating that Nanyang Shipping Company would use the land in dispute to offset the debt of Hainan Success Company. Liu Wentao, who represented Nanyang Shipping Company in signing the Repayment Guarantee Agreement with Chen Lin, testified in another criminal case: "Before signing the above documents, he and Chen Lin knew that the land in dispute was not Nanyang Shipping’s land, indicating that the debt-to-asset swap was also malicious."

Appellant Hainan Success Company, in response to the appeal requests and reasons of appellant Nanyang Real Estate Company, submitted its defense: 1. It agrees with the facts and reasons stated by Nanyang Real Estate Company in its appeal petition and agrees with all of Nanyang Real Estate Company’s appeal requests. 2. The judgment of first instance was erroneous in finding that Nanyang Real Estate Company does not enjoy the land use right for the land in dispute. (a) Under the premise that neither Nanyang Real Estate Company nor Nanyang Shipping Company has obtained the state-owned land use right certificate for the land in dispute, the subject that approved the relevant administrative documents and the subject that invested in the land in dispute should serve as the basis for determining the owner of the land use right. The land in dispute was lawfully approved and acquired by Nanyang Real Estate Company. Although no state-owned land use right certificate was obtained, the relevant approval procedures for the transfer of the land in dispute, the state-owned land use right transfer contract, and the land allocation agreement were all handled or signed by Nanyang Real Estate Company; the land transfer fee, land acquisition fee, infrastructure construction costs, and other expenses for the land in dispute were all borne and paid by Nanyang Real Estate Company; other land within the development zone where the land in dispute is located was also developed and directly disposed of by Nanyang Real Estate Company, and the land use right was processed by the land department to the name of the transferee. Nanyang Real Estate Company followed the above method to handle state-owned land use right certificates for Hainan Nanhai Natural Gas Engineering Co., Ltd. and a large number of natural persons. Therefore, the judgment of first instance should not have excluded Nanyang Real Estate Company’s legitimate rights and interests in the land in dispute on the ground that it did not obtain the land use right certificate. (b) The land in dispute is merely a piece of land that was segregated during the enforcement process to match the "loan of RMB 2 million." It is not land with separate approval documents or a transfer contract. When confirming the ownership of the land in dispute, it should be determined based on the administrative approval documents and capital investment situation of the entire project land where the land in dispute is located. The judgment of first instance erroneously severed the relationship between the land in dispute and other land in the project and failed to adopt evidence that could directly or indirectly prove the ownership of the land in dispute. (c) There is no dispute among all parties that the land in dispute is part of the land acquired under the Land Acquisition (Allocation) Agreement dated June 24, 1995. The judgment of first instance erroneously found that it was "not proven that the land in dispute is the land acquired in the Land Acquisition (Allocation) Agreement dated June 24, 1995." (d) The statements of the Dongfang City People’s Government of Hainan Province in the administrative case were entirely derived from the Civil Mediation Agreement (2003) Wu Qu Shui Min Chu Zi No. 265 of the Wuchang District People’s Court. The act of the Dongfang City land department in handling the land certificate was an act of assisting enforcement and cannot serve as the basis for determining the ownership of the land in dispute. (e) In 2002, the Dongfang City Bureau of Land and Resources of Hainan Province issued a notice of intended land recovery, which found that the relevant land use right belonged to Nanyang Real Estate Company. As of the end of 2001, there were no intangible assets (land use rights are intangible assets) on the books of Nanyang Shipping Company. This evidence all corroborates that Nanyang Shipping Company did not own any land and proves that the land in dispute belongs to Nanyang Real Estate Company. Therefore, the historical evolution of Nanyang Real Estate Company did not cause it to lose its rights to the project land in the Basuo Development Zone and even to the land in dispute. In summary, the judgment of first instance finding that Nanyang Real Estate Company has no right to claim the land use right for the land in dispute constitutes an error in fact finding. 3. The finding of the court of first instance that the loan relationship was true was erroneous. The legal relationship of the loan between Hainan Success Company and Chen Lin is the core disputed issue in this case, but the court of first instance failed to perform a reasonable duty of review, did not ascertain the relevant facts, and directly caused the error in the judgment of first instance.

Appellant Hainan Success Company’s appeal requests: 1. To set aside the Civil Judgment (2018) E Min Chu No. 77 of the Hubei High People’s Court in accordance with the law; 2. To set aside the Civil Judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of the Hubei High People’s Court in accordance with the law; 3. To amend the judgment to confirm that the state-owned land use right currently registered in the name of Chen Lin under Dongfang Guo Yong (2003) No. 383 and the state-owned land use right contributed by Chen Lin and currently registered in the name of Hainan Jincan Company under Dongfang Guo Yong (2012) No. 076 belong to Nanyang Real Estate Company; 4. To have Chen Lin bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Facts and reasons: 1. The judgment of first instance failed to strictly examine the authenticity of the loan relationship and erroneously found that the loan relationship truly existed and had been performed. (a) Chen Lin should bear the burden of proof for the establishment and performance of the RMB 2 million loan relationship he claimed. The judgment of first instance found the loan relationship established merely based on the authenticity of the company seal on the IOU, ignoring the facts that the signature of "Fan Yunhai" on the IOU was forged, Chen Lin’s statements in the various court hearings about personally seeing Fan Yunhai sign the IOU were contradictory, and Chen Lin was unable to provide any payment vouchers or transaction records, leading to an erroneous finding on whether the loan relationship was true. (b) The judgment of first instance presumed that Nanyang Shipping Company’s account was frozen during the restructuring period and, based on the principle that laws are not retroactive, found that the loan relationship existed and had been actually performed. This lacks factual and legal basis and contains obvious logical flaws. (c) The judgment of first instance stated: "(Chen Lin and Hainan Jincan Company) have no objection to the authenticity of the eighth group of evidence but do not accept its purpose of proof." Thus, Chen Lin had no objection to the authenticity of the record of his interview by the Economic Investigation Division of the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department, yet the judgment of first instance did not accept the authenticity of the above confession, which is contradictory. (d) The judgment of first instance failed to cautiously examine the facts of the loan, contravening the guiding spirit of the Supreme People’s Court in preventing and sanctioning false litigation. 2. The judgment of first instance was erroneous in finding that Nanyang Real Estate Company has no right to claim the land use right for the land in dispute. (a) The time for the development and consolidation of the land in dispute was between 1994 and 1997. At that time, the procedures for state-owned land development were not as complete and orderly as they are now. Failure to obtain a land use right certificate should not be a reason to exclude Nanyang Real Estate Company’s legitimate rights and interests in the land in dispute. (b) Nanyang Real Estate Company has paid all but RMB 328,000 of the outstanding balance of the state-owned land use right transfer fee and land acquisition fee for the land in dispute and has made substantial investments in the surrounding infrastructure of the land in dispute. It should be found that the land in dispute belongs to Nanyang Real Estate Company. (c) The erroneous finding of the Dongfang City Land and Resources Department of Hainan Province on the ownership of the land in dispute stemmed from the Civil Mediation Agreement (2003) Wu Qu Shui Min Chu Zi No. 265 of the Wuchang District People’s Court of Wuhan City, Hubei Province. Therefore, the statements of the Dongfang City People’s Government of Hainan Province in the administrative litigation case are insufficient to serve as the basis for determining the ownership of the land in dispute. (d) After March 8, 1997, the land in dispute always belonged to Nanyang Real Estate Company. First, the Advance Notice on Intended Recovery of Occupied Land (2002) of the Dongfang City Bureau of Land and Environmental Resources of Hainan Province indicates that in 2002, the Dongfang City Bureau of Land and Resources of Hainan Province still found that the land under Approval No. (1994) 26 belonged to Nanyang Real Estate Company. Second, based on the audit reports and annual reports of Nanyang Shipping Company provided by Hainan Success Company, as of the end of 2001, there were no intangible assets such as land use rights (land use rights are intangible assets) on the books of Nanyang Shipping Company, proving that Nanyang Shipping Company did not own any project land. Furthermore, according to the restructuring arrangement between Nanyang Shipping Company and Hainan Success Company, in 2001, Nanyang Shipping Company transferred all non-cash, non-accounts receivable assets, including equity in Nanyang Real Estate Company, to Hainan Success Company. If Nanyang Shipping Company had owned the land in dispute before the transfer, the land in dispute would also have been transferred to Hainan Success Company. After 2001, Nanyang Shipping Company would have no right to claim that it owned the relevant land, let alone have the right to use it as its own property to offset debts in 2003. Therefore, Nanyang Real Estate Company’s rights to the project land, including the land in dispute, were not affected during the process in which it lost and then restored its independent legal personality.

Appellant Nanyang Real Estate Company agreed with the appeal requests and reasons of appellant Hainan Success Company.

Appellee Nanyang Shipping Company, in response to the appeal requests of appellants Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company, submitted a joint defense: It agrees with all appeal requests raised by Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company in their appeal petitions and supports all claims in the complaint of Nanyang Real Estate Company. 1. It should be found that the loan in dispute was fabricated. The mediation between Nanyang Shipping Company and Chen Lin was conducted under circumstances where the official seal of Nanyang Shipping Company and the financial seal of Hainan Success Company were both controlled by Liu Wentao. Liu Wentao himself was sentenced to a criminal penalty for embezzlement from Nanyang Shipping Company. According to the appraisal report of the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department (the same appraisal finding that Fan Yunhai’s signature was forged), Liu Wentao himself also used the official seal of Nanyang Shipping Company and the financial seal of Hainan Success Company to forge IOU documents and forge documents with Fan Yunhai’s signature, creating fictitious loans for the relevant companies in his own name. The IOU held by Chen Lin, like other documents where Fan Yunhai’s signature was found to be forged by appraisal, exhibits the situation where the seal is genuine but the signature is false. It is highly likely that the IOU in dispute was fabricated by Liu Wentao, using his convenience of holding the financial seal of Hainan Success Company, in collusion with Chen Lin, to forge Fan Yunhai’s signature. This defective IOU cannot serve as evidence of the occurrence of the RMB 2 million loan. Additionally, Chen Lin, as the lender, made contradictory statements on different occasions regarding whether the loan occurred and how the IOU was signed, including an instance where Chen Lin himself admitted that the loan did not actually occur. His several statements about Fan Yunhai signing the IOU in person were inconsistent with the appraisal conclusion that the signature was forged. Apart from the seriously defective IOU, although Chen Lin stated in court that there were various human and material witnesses and that he was capable of providing evidence, he was unable to provide any material or human evidence to prove the actual occurrence of the loan in his formal evidence submission. Given the huge amount of the so-called "loan," his statements and inability to provide evidence are clearly contrary to common sense and should lead to the presumption that the loan was fictitious. Even if the mediation matter in the original trial is not found to be false litigation, it should be found that Chen Lin failed to meet his burden of proof, that the loan matter does not exist, and the judgment should be amended. 2. The finding of the court of first instance on the ownership of the land in dispute was erroneous. The relevant approvals for the land in dispute, the state-owned land use right transfer contract, and the land allocation agreement were all processed in the name of Nanyang Real Estate Company. They were never renamed or transferred to Nanyang Shipping Company. The various expenditures, fees, and state-owned land use right transfer fees related to the land in dispute were also borne and paid by Nanyang Real Estate Company and are unrelated to Nanyang Shipping Company. Nanyang Shipping Company never obtained any authorization from Nanyang Real Estate Company for the disposal of the land in dispute. When Liu Wentao disposed of the land in dispute to Chen Lin in the name of Nanyang Shipping Company, he did not seek any opinions within Nanyang Shipping Company regarding the ownership or disposal of the land. At the time of the land disposal, Nanyang Shipping Company only held 2% of the equity in Nanyang Real Estate Company. According to Liu Wentao’s own statement and the description of the land department officials, Liu Wentao used means to confuse Nanyang Shipping Company with Nanyang Real Estate Company to transfer the land in dispute to Chen Lin.

Appellees Chen Lin and Hainan Jincan Company jointly responded to the appeal requests of Appellants Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company as follows: 1. The source of the involved loan of RMB 2 million was savings from many years of business, proceeds of RMB 480,000 from the sale of his sister's house in Shanghai, and funds borrowed from relatives and friends. The loan was paid in cash in three installments, with the final payment consolidated into one IOU, because all of the other party's bank accounts had been frozen. At that time, the local government did not wish for Nanyang Shipping Company to be delisted, and Nanyang Shipping Company owned land, so the risk was relatively small. They resolved the debt issue through litigation, mediation, and enforcement in the Wuchang District Court. The contract stipulated that 100 mu of land would be used to offset the debt, but the Dongfang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources still completed the judicial enforcement through administrative procedures such as land appraisal and signing a land transfer contract, ultimately only 60.9 mu being used to offset the debt. 2. During the period of acquiring the involved land, Nanyang Shipping Company subdivided the land into smaller plots and transferred them to third parties, amounting to dozens of transactions over several years, some of which led to litigation. Judicial decisions confirmed the legality of Nanyang Shipping Company's transfer of the land, but Nanyang Real Estate Company never asserted any rights over the land. 3. The oral statement transcript made during criminal detention was made under conditions of deprivation of personal freedom and subject to extortion of confessions by torture, and did not represent true intent. After investigation, the public security organ determined that the alleged misappropriation or fraud of the RMB 2 million was not established and closed the case. The closure of the case itself fully demonstrates that the RMB 2 million loan was genuine. 3. In the appraisal report on the IOU made during the public security organ's investigation, the source of the "original handwriting of Fan Yunhai" in the test material was unclear. 4. Nanyang Real Estate Company does not have the right to use the involved land. In the 1990s, Nanyang Shipping Company reached an agreement with the local government for the contiguous development of 2,005 mu of land, which was merely operated through its subsidiary Nanyang Real Estate Company. All initial land development investment and proceeds were entirely attributable to the parent company, Nanyang Shipping Company. It did not pay the land transfer fee for the 2,005 mu, nor did it pay the land transfer fee for the 60.9 mu in this case. After 1995, Nanyang Real Estate Company essentially withdrew from the development of this land. Subsequently, due to the delisting crisis faced by Nanyang Shipping Company, with approval from higher-level government, 460 mu of land was allocated to Nanyang Shipping Company and transferred to third parties. The above situation can be verified through investigation with government departments. Nanyang Shipping Company transferred the land to third parties, and the Dongfang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources handled the procedures. Some land transactions led to litigation, and judicial decisions confirmed the legality of the land transfers between the parties. Nanyang Real Estate Company is neither the land use rights holder nor does it have any connection to the land. Furthermore, even if Nanyang Shipping Company had offset its land with Chen Lin's debt and lawfully handled the land transfer procedures and obtained the land use right certificate, Chen Lin would be a bona fide third party. If Nanyang Real Estate Company believes its rights have been infringed, it should claim damages from Nanyang Shipping Company, not from Chen Lin, and certainly cannot deny the legality of the debt-offset agreement. Moreover, the people's court cannot, in a third-party opposition action for infringement, review and rule on the validity of the involved debt-offset agreement or the legal effect of the Dongfang Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources' handling of the land transfer and issuance of the land use right certificate to Chen Lin. In summary, Nanyang Real Estate Company has no rights to the land. It is neither a third party within the meaning of the legislative purpose of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China nor the holder of rights to the involved land. It has no standing to bring this lawsuit, and this action should be dismissed.

Nanyang Real Estate Company filed a lawsuit with the Hubei High People's Court, requesting: 1. Reversal of Civil Judgment No. (2015) E-Min-Jian-San-Zai-Zhong-00008 of that court; 2. Confirmation that the state-owned land use right under certificate Dong Fang Guo Yong (2003) No. 383 registered in the name of Chen Lin, and the state-owned land use right under certificate Dong Fang Guo Yong (2012) No. 076, which was contributed by Chen Lin as capital and is currently registered in the name of Hainan Jincan Commercial Trading Co., Ltd., belong to Nanyang Real Estate Company; 3. Litigation costs of this case to be borne by Chen Lin. If, during trial, the court finds that after the reversal of Civil Judgment No. (2015) E-Min-Jian-San-Zai-Zhong-00008, other judgments also need to be modified, Nanyang Real Estate Company may cooperate with the court to amend its claims.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On March 31, 1994, the People's Government of Dongfang Li Autonomous County (later renamed Dongfang City, Hainan Province) issued Document Dong Fu Fu [1994] No. 26 approving the reply to the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, which: 1. Approved the transfer of the third residential zone of Basuo Development Zone to Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company for development, with boundaries: east to Third Ring Road, north to Donghai Second Road, south to Zhengfa Road, west to the building boundary, with an actual land area of approximately 2,205 mu (subject to the red line plan); 2. Approved the basic land transfer price to average RMB 18,000 per mu (including compensation for green seedlings, excluding costs for relocation of graves, compensation for houses and buildings). The price for planned roads was to be collected at the average land transfer price, with a transfer term of seventy years; 3. The transferred plots included a planned primary school land area of 90 mu, reserved by the county government for a future primary school site. The land acquisition fees and compensation costs were to be deducted from the land transfer fees for Zone 3. The primary school land would no longer bear the costs of "three connections and one leveling" development. After development of Zone 3 was completed, it was to be delivered to the county government for use as a school; 4. The procedures for land use approval must be completed before handling the land transfer procedures; 5. All relevant documents and contracts for joint development previously signed between the county government and Nanyang Shipping Company, as well as other unit agreements signed within the development zone, were to be withdrawn and nullified.

On April 3, 1994, the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County and Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company signed the "Contract for the Transfer of Land Use Rights for Continuous Development in Dongfang Li Autonomous County," agreeing that the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County would transfer the land use rights for plot number three in the third residential zone of Basuo Development Zone, with an area of 1,470,007 square meters, to Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company. The term of the land use rights transfer was seventy years, commencing from the date of issuance of the "State-Owned Land Use Right Certificate of the People's Republic of China" for the plot. Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company agreed to pay to the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County in accordance with the contract the land transfer fee, land use fee, and land value-added tax upon transfer to a third party. The land transfer fee for this plot was RMB 26.99 per square meter, totaling RMB 39,675,488.9. Within thirty days of the signing of this contract, Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company was required to pay 5% of the total land transfer fee, totaling RMB 1,983,774.44, in cashier's check or cash to the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County as a performance deposit. Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company was to pay the full land transfer fee within sixty days of signing the contract. If payment was not made in full within the time limit, the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County had the right to terminate the contract and seek compensation for breach of contract. Within ten days after paying the full land transfer fee to the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company was to complete the land registration procedures in accordance with regulations and obtain the "State-Owned Land Use Right Certificate of the People's Republic of China," thereby acquiring the land use rights.

On May 16, 1995, the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County issued the "Red Line Plan for the Construction of Land for the Continuous Development of Land Transfer by Nanyang Shipping in Basuo," determining that the total area of the above-mentioned transferred land was 1,969.58 mu, road area 289.8 mu, and actual land area 1,697.78 mu.

On July 23, 1994, the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, the Basuo Town Basuo Management District of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, and Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company signed the "Agreement on Land Expropriation (Allocation)." The agreement indicated: Construction project: continuous development; Expropriating (allocating) unit: Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County; Expropriated (allocated) unit: Basuo Town Basuo Management District, Dongfang County; Land use unit: Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company; Content: Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company, for the construction of the continuous development project, needed to expropriate 3.036 hectares of land located in the area east of Zhengfa Road in Basuo Management District. The total land compensation and resettlement subsidy was RMB 542,500. The prices for the expropriated paddy fields and dry fields were to be further negotiated between the government and Nanyang Shipping Company. On July 23, 1994, the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, the Julong Management District of Basuo Town, Dongfang Li Autonomous County, and Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company signed the "Agreement on Land Expropriation (Allocation)." The agreement indicated: Construction project: continuous development; Expropriating (allocating) unit: Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County; Expropriated (allocated) unit: Julong Management District, Basuo Town, Dongfang County; Land use unit: Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company; Content: Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company, for the construction of the continuous development project, needed to expropriate 0.662 hectares of land located in the area east of Zhengfa Road in Julong Management District. II. At the trial of first instance, Chen Lin stated regarding how the RMB 2 million was paid to Hainan Success Company: "I paid it in three installments, all in cash." (When was it paid?) "To Fan Yunhai" (the former chairman of Hainan Success Company). (Where was it paid?) "I do not remember the exact time. Once at a hotel, once at a restaurant, and once when he came to pick me up, I gave it to him." (Which hotel?) "Qiongyuan Hotel." (Which payment was made at the hotel?) "I do not remember which one specifically. I only remember three locations. Another time was at a shark fin restaurant during dinner." (Where was the remaining payment made?) "In the car from Meilan Airport to the hotel." (Why did you not transfer the money and instead pay in cash?) "At that time, Nanyang Group and (Hainan) Success Company were going to be delisted. They had no accounts (the accounts were frozen). The company's accounts could no longer be used." (Then why did you not transfer to a personal account?) "Because I lent it to the company. At that time, he told me the company needed to pay salaries and the like. Moreover, we had previously had fund transfers using cash. He was also hiding from creditors everywhere, so I gave him cash." (Did he issue a receipt each time?) "He issued receipts for the first two times. The last time, he took back the previous two receipts and exchanged them for the current IOU." (Where did you get the RMB 2 million?) "Part of it was money I earned from business, and part was from selling a house in Shanghai." (Whose house was sold?) "My sister Chen Bin's house in Shanghai." (When was it sold?) "In April 2002." (How much was it sold for?) "RMB 480,000." (Was this RMB 480,000 part of the RMB 2 million? How much of your own money was there?) "I had over RMB 300,000, my wife had over RMB 100,000, and I also borrowed some from friends. In addition, my father-in-law used his own money and money borrowed from neighbors. I still have not repaid some of it to this day." (Are there IOUs for these?) "Some have them. If necessary, I can submit them to the court. During the process of repayment, my father-in-law passed away. I even carried my father-in-law to the court. Many creditors were present at that time, and many people from your court can testify."

The original court held that, based on the facts of the case and the parties' allegations and defenses, the issues in dispute at first instance and the analysis thereof were as follows:

1. Regarding whether the subject qualification of Nanyang Real Estate Company in filing this third-party revocation action was lawful. The court held that Chen Lin and Hainan Jincan Company argued that the subject qualification of Nanyang Real Estate Company was unlawful, primarily asserting that Nanyang Real Estate Company's business license was revoked in 2004 and was not restored until 2013, and the shareholders before and after the restoration were different. Therefore, the Nanyang Real Estate Company after 2013 had no relationship with the previous Nanyang Real Estate Company, and its subject qualification was unlawful. The court held that, according to the provisions of the "Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Determine the Civil Litigation Status After the Business License of an Enterprise Legal Person Is Revoked" (Fa Jing [2000] No. 24, January 29, 2000), the revocation of the business license of an enterprise legal person is an administrative penalty imposed by the administrative authority for industry and commerce on a violating enterprise legal person in accordance with national industrial and commercial administration regulations. From the time the business license of an enterprise legal person is revoked until it is deregistered, the enterprise legal person shall still be deemed to exist and may engage in litigation activities in its own name. In this case, based on the evidence submitted by Chen Lin, Nanyang Real Estate Company had only had its business license revoked by the administrative department for industry and commerce, but had not been deregistered. Therefore, the civil litigation status of Nanyang Real Estate Company had always continued to exist. Article 72 of the Company Law of the PRC provides that "Shareholders of a limited liability company may transfer all or part of their equity to each other... Where the company's articles of association have other provisions on equity transfer, such provisions shall prevail." This shows that the transfer of a company's equity only needs to be changed through statutory or agreed procedures. The registration of a change in a company's equity is an administrative licensing act performed by the administrative authority for industry and commerce upon application by the party and after examination according to law. Its legal effect is to confirm the party's subject qualification in the company and to have the effect of public summons for the exercise of relevant civil acts. A change in the company's shareholders does not result in the extinction of the company's legal personality, meaning its civil litigation status does not change. Therefore, the defense of Chen Lin and Hainan Jincan Company that the civil litigation status of Nanyang Real Estate Company was unlawful could not be established, and the court did not support it.

2. Regarding whether Nanyang Real Estate Company filed this third-party revocation action within the statutory period. The court held that Article 56 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (2012 Revision) provides: "If a third party considers that it has an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties, it has the right to file a lawsuit. If a third party does not have an independent claim to the subject matter of the litigation between the parties, but the outcome of the case has a legal interest for it, it may apply to participate in the proceedings, or the people's court may notify it to participate in the proceedings. A third party for whom the people's court's judgment bears civil liability has the litigation rights and obligations of a party. If a third party as provided in the preceding two paragraphs fails to participate in the proceedings for reasons not attributable to itself, but has evidence proving that part or all of the content of a legally effective judgment, ruling, or mediation document is erroneous and damages its civil rights and interests, it may, within six months from the date it knew or should have known that its civil rights and interests were damaged, file a lawsuit with the people's court that made the judgment, ruling, or mediation document. After trial, if the lawsuit claim is established, the people's court shall alter or revoke the original judgment, ruling, or mediation document; if the lawsuit claim is not established, the claim shall be dismissed." In this case, Nanyang Real Estate Company claimed that the content of the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court was erroneous and damaged its civil rights and interests. As a third party, it was unable to participate in the proceedings of the case (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 for reasons not attributable to itself, and thus filed a revocation action with this court, requesting the revocation of the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court. The civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court was rendered on April 22, 2015. Nanyang Real Estate Company filed this third-party revocation action with this court on October 14, 2015, which did not exceed the six-month period provided in the above article. Therefore, the filing of this third-party revocation action by Nanyang Real Estate Company was within the statutory period. The argument of Chen Lin and Hainan Jincan Company that the period for Nanyang Real Estate Company to file a revocation action should be calculated from the date of the civil judgment (2011) Wu Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 00097 of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province on July 29, 2011, lacked legal basis, and the court did not support it.

3. Regarding whether Nanyang Real Estate Company had the right to use the land involved in the case. The court held that the land involved in the case was state-owned land. Both the provision in Article 9, paragraph 2 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC (1988 Revision) that "State-owned land used lawfully by units under ownership by the whole people, units under collective ownership, and individuals shall be registered with the local people's government at or above the county level, which shall issue a certificate to confirm the right to use," and the provision in Article 11, paragraph 3 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC (1998 Revision) and the Land Administration Law of the PRC (2004 Revision) that "State-owned land used lawfully by units and individuals shall be registered with the people's government at or above the county level, which shall issue a certificate to confirm the right to use," indicate that state-owned land used lawfully by units and individuals shall be registered with the people's government at or above the county level, which shall issue a certificate to confirm the right to use. Nanyang Real Estate Company claimed that it had the right to use the land involved in the case, but it only provided the document Dong Fu Fu [1994] No. 26, dated March 31, 1994, in which the People's Government of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province agreed to transfer the land including the land involved in the case to Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company, and the "Contract for the Transfer of the Right to Use Land for Piecemeal Development in Dongfang Li Autonomous County" signed on April 3, 1994, between the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province and Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company. It did not provide evidence proving that it had paid the land transfer fee, nor did it provide evidence proving that it had obtained the state-owned land use right certificate for the land involved in the case. Moreover, in the administrative litigation case where Nanyang Real Estate Company sued the People's Government of Dongfang City, Hainan Province for issuing a certificate to Chen Lin, the People's Government of Dongfang City, Hainan Province also explicitly stated that the right to use the land involved in the case belonged to Nanyang Shipping Company. The "Land Expropriation (Allocation) Agreements" submitted by Nanyang Real Estate Company, signed on July 23, 1994, and June 24, 1995, respectively, between Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company and the Basuo Management Area of Basuo Town, Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province, the Julong Management Area of Basuo Town, Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province, the Daoxi Forest Farm of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province, the Huangning Management Area of Basuo Town, Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province, and the Basuo Management Area of Basuo Town, Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province, could only prove that Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company had previously signed agreements for land expropriation for development projects. Nanyang Real Estate Company did not submit evidence proving that the land involved in the case was the land agreed to be requisitioned in the "Land Expropriation (Allocation) Agreement" signed on June 24, 1995, with the Basuo Management Area of Basuo Town, Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province. Relying solely on that agreement could not prove that the land involved in the case was requisitioned by Nanyang Real Estate Company. The voucher No. 6 dated January 22, 1997, and the voucher No. 6 dated April 30, 1997, submitted by Nanyang Real Estate Company, were both payment vouchers of Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd. Nanyang Real Estate Company also did not submit evidence proving that the land requisition payment recorded in the payment vouchers was paid for the land involved in the case. Relying solely on those payment vouchers could not prove that the land requisition payment for the land involved in the case was paid by Nanyang Real Estate Company. The land in this case was state-owned transferred land. Even if Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company had previously requisitioned the land involved in the case and paid the land requisition payment, because the nature of the land requisition payment and the state-owned land transfer fee are different, the payment of the land requisition payment for the land involved in the case by Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company could not replace the payment of the land transfer fee. The above evidence also could not prove that Nanyang Real Estate Company had the right to use the land involved in the case. Moreover, on March 8, 1997, Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company was approved by the industrial and commercial authority to change its name to "Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd. Real Estate Company", becoming a branch of "Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd.", and lost its independent legal personality. Even if Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company had previously signed the "Contract for the Transfer of the Right to Use Land for Piecemeal Development in Dongfang Li Autonomous County" and paid the land transfer fee for the land involved in the case, the contractual rights and obligations thereafter would be enjoyed and borne by the parent company of Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd. Real Estate Company, namely Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd. and Nanyang Shipping Company after its name change. On July 18, 2001, the enterprise name of "Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd. Real Estate Company" was changed to "Nanyang Shipping Group Co., Ltd. Real Estate Branch". On August 13, 2001, when Nanyang Shipping Group Co., Ltd. Real Estate Branch changed its name to "Nanyang Real Estate Company" with a capital contribution of RMB 400,000 from Nanyang Shipping Company and RMB 19.6 million from Hainan Success Company, Nanyang Shipping Company only contributed RMB 400,000 in cash and did not contribute the right to use the land involved in the case or other corresponding rights as capital to Nanyang Real Estate Company. Nanyang Real Estate Company had no right to claim the right to use the land involved in the case. Therefore, Nanyang Real Estate Company's claim that it had the right to use the land involved in the case lacked factual and legal basis.

4. Regarding whether the content of the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 was erroneous and whether it damaged the interests of Nanyang Real Estate Company. The court held that, according to Article 296 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC", which provides that "Part or all of the content of the judgments, rulings, and mediation documents referred to in Article 56, paragraph 3 of the Civil Procedure Law means the main text of judgments and rulings, and the result of handling the civil rights and obligations of the parties in mediation documents," Nanyang Real Estate Company claimed that the content of the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court was erroneous and damaged its civil rights and interests. It should provide evidence proving that the result of handling the civil rights and obligations between Nanyang Shipping Company, Hainan Success Company, and Chen Lin in the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court was erroneous, and that such error damaged its civil rights and interests. The result of handling the civil rights and obligations between Nanyang Shipping Company, Hainan Success Company, and Chen Lin in the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court was to uphold the civil judgment (2011) Wu Min Zai Zhong Zi No. 00097 of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court of Hubei Province, which was to uphold the civil mediation document (2003) Wu Qu Shui Min Chu Zi No. 265 of the Wuchang District People's Court of Wuhan, Hubei Province. The content of that civil mediation document was that Nanyang Shipping Company would transfer to Chen Lin the right to use the 100 mu of land located within the Basuo Development Zone of Nanyang Shipping Group, Dongfang City, Hainan Province (west of Erhuan Road, south of Yuanlin Road, north of Jiefang Road) to offset its guarantee obligation of RMB 2 million in principal and RMB 110,000 in interest originally undertaken for Hainan Success Company. It did not involve the rights and obligations of Nanyang Real Estate Company and did not damage the civil rights and interests of Nanyang Real Estate Company.

Regarding whether the loan relationship between Chen Lin and Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company was genuine. The court held that Nanyang Real Estate Company was not a party to the above loan relationship. Whether the loan relationship was genuine should be resolved by the parties to the loan relationship through retrial procedures, and it was not within the scope of trial of this revocation action. However, considering the grounds on which the Supreme People's Court remanded the case for retrial, this court also examined the authenticity of the above loan relationship. On May 15, 2002, Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company issued an IOU to Chen Lin, recording the facts of the loan relationship and the corresponding guarantee measures, and affixing the financial seal of Hainan Success Company and the official seal of Nanyang Shipping Company. On March 10, 2003, Liu Wentao, then vice president of Nanyang Shipping Company, signed on the above IOU stating "Confirm all of the above content" and affixed the official seal. The official seal of an enterprise legal person is the legal stamp for the enterprise legal person to confirm the establishment of its expression of intent externally. For a contract affixed with a genuine seal, the rights and obligations thereunder shall be borne by the entity that affixed the seal. Although the signature of "Fan Yunhai" on the IOU was found to be forged upon expert examination, the financial seal of Hainan Success Company affixed was found to be genuine upon expert examination. According to Article 32 of the Contract Law of the PRC, which provides that "A contract is established when the parties sign or affix their seals to the contract in written form," the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court found the IOU in this case to be genuine and the establishment of the loan relationship to be proper. Nanyang Real Estate Company, Hainan Success Company, and Nanyang Shipping Company all argued that the RMB 2 million loan was not genuine. Hainan Success Company claimed it had not received the RMB 2 million loan. However, Chen Lin stated during the trial that at that time, because Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company were required by the regulatory authority to delist, their fund accounts were all frozen. At the request of Fan Yunhai, the former chairman of Hainan Success Company, the RMB 2 million in cash was handed over to Fan Yunhai in three installments. Combined with the relevant evidence submitted by Nanyang Real Estate Company, Hainan Success Company, and Nanyang Shipping Company, it can be confirmed that during the payment period described by Chen Lin, Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company were indeed undergoing asset restructuring, and Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company did not deny the fact that their fund accounts were frozen during the asset restructuring period. Moreover, the above loan occurred in 2002, and it is not appropriate to apply the relevant provisions of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases" which came into effect on September 1, 2015. Therefore, in terms of the probative force of the evidence, Chen Lin's claim that there was a loan relationship of RMB 2 million between himself and Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company and that it had been actually performed was reasonable. The reason for Nanyang Real Estate Company's argument that the RMB 2 million loan was not genuine could not be established, and the court did not support it. Regarding the issue of Chen Lin's inconsistent statements about the loan facts during the investigation by the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department, because those oral statements were not confirmed by the relevant judicial authorities, and the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department did not make a negative determination on the loan facts based on the above investigation and subsequently pursue criminal prosecution against Chen Lin, the court did not recognize the authenticity of the above oral statements. Therefore, Nanyang Real Estate Company's claim that it had the right to use the 100 mu of land involved in the case, and that the civil judgment (2015) E Min Jian San Zai Zhong Zi No. 00008 of this court, which upheld the rights and obligations determined in the original effective legal document that Nanyang Shipping Company should satisfy the debt to Chen Lin by transferring the above 100 mu of land, was erroneous and infringed upon its civil rights and interests, could not be established, and the court did not support it.

In summary, the litigation claims of Nanyang Real Estate Company lacked factual and legal basis. Pursuant to Article 56 and Article 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 300 of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC", this court rendered the following judgment: The litigation claims of Nanyang Real Estate Company were dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 23,680 was to be borne by Nanyang Real Estate Company.

During the second instance of this court, Nanyang Real Estate Company submitted the civil judgment (2019) Qiong Min Zhong No. 113 rendered by the Hainan High People's Court on May 20, 2019, to prove that another shareholder of Hainan Jincan Company, Luo Changren, held 49% of the equity of that company on behalf of Chen Lin. That judgment determined that the equity nominee holding relationship between Chen Lin and Luo Changren was terminated, and the 49% equity would be transferred to Chen Lin's name, making Chen Lin the sole shareholder of Hainan Jincan Company.

The second instance of this court confirmed the facts found by the original trial.

This court held that, based on the parties' appeal requests and defense opinions, the issues in dispute in this second instance were: whether the original trial correctly determined that Nanyang Real Estate Company did not have the right to use the land involved in the case; and whether the RMB 2 million loan between Chen Lin and Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company was genuinely existing.

I. Whether Nanyang Real Estate Company enjoys the land use right involved in this case.

This Court holds that, according to the provisions of Article 9, Paragraph 2 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC as revised on December 29, 1988, which states: "For state-owned land lawfully used by units of ownership by the whole people, units of collective ownership, and individuals, the local people's government at or above the county level shall register, compile a register, and issue a certificate to confirm the right of use," and Article 11, Paragraph 3 of the Land Administration Law of the PRC as revised on August 29, 1998, which states: "For state-owned land lawfully used by units and individuals, the people's government at or above the county level shall register, compile a register, and issue a certificate to confirm the right of use," the lawful use of state-owned land requires registration procedures and obtaining relevant certificates from the people's government at or above the county level to confirm the land use right.

First, in this case, Nanyang Real Estate Company failed to provide evidence showing that it had paid the land transfer fee for the land in question or that it had obtained the state-owned land use right certificate for the land in question. The documents it submitted -- namely, the Dongfu Fu [1994] No. 26 document dated March 31, 1994, in which the People's Government of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province agreed to transfer the land in question and other land to Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company, and the "Contract for the Grant of Land Use Rights for Piecemeal Development between the Land Administration Bureau of Dongfang Li Autonomous County, Hainan Province and Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company" dated April 3, 1994 -- are insufficient to prove that it already owned the land use right in question.

Second, in the administrative lawsuit filed by Nanyang Real Estate Company against the People's Government of Dongfang City, Hainan Province for issuing a certificate to Chen Lin, the People's Government of Dongfang City, Hainan Province expressly stated that the land use right in question belonged to Nanyang Shipping Company. The "Agreement on Land Acquisition (Allocation)" submitted by Nanyang Real Estate Company can only prove that Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company had once entered into an agreement for land acquisition for a development project, but is insufficient to prove that the land in question had been acquired by Nanyang Real Estate Company. Furthermore, the "Payment Voucher No. 6" dated January 22, 1997, and the "Payment Voucher No. 6" dated April 30, 1997, submitted by Nanyang Real Estate Company, are both payment vouchers of Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd., and cannot prove that the land acquisition fees indicated in those vouchers were paid for the land in question.

Third, because the land in question is state-owned granted land, even if Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company had previously acquired it and paid the land acquisition fees, since the nature of land acquisition fees and state-owned land grant fees are different, the payment of land acquisition fees for the land in question by Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company cannot substitute for the payment of the land grant fee. Therefore, the appellate arguments of Nanyang Real Estate Company that "it enjoys the land use right in question by reason of having paid the land acquisition fee" and of Hainan Success Company that "the land development and consolidation of the land in question occurred between 1994 and 1997, and at that time the state-owned land development process was not as complete and orderly as it is now, so the failure to obtain a land use right certificate should not be used to exclude Nanyang Real Estate Company's lawful rights and interests in the land in question," cannot be sustained.

Fourth, this case has established that on March 8, 1997, Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company was approved by the industrial and commercial authority to change its name to "Real Estate Company of Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd.," becoming a "branch of Hainan Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd.," thereby losing its status as an independent legal person. All debts and claims pertaining to that company should be wholly attributed to its parent company, "Nanyang Shipping Industrial Co., Ltd.," and to the subsequently renamed "Nanyang Shipping Company." Even if "Hainan Nanyang Shipping Real Estate Company" had enjoyed the land use right in question, after it lost its legal person status, that right should be enjoyed by Nanyang Shipping Company.

Fifth, on August 13, 2001, Nanyang Shipping Company made a monetary capital contribution of RMB 400,000 and Hainan Success Company made a monetary capital contribution of RMB 19,600,000 to establish Nanyang Real Estate Company. Nanyang Shipping Company only contributed RMB 400,000 in cash and did not contribute the land use right in question or any corresponding other rights as capital to Nanyang Real Estate Company.

Sixth, this case has also established that the land in question was not an asset of Nanyang Real Estate Company at the time of its establishment in 2001. Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company did not provide evidence proving that Nanyang Real Estate Company subsequently acquired the land use right in question. Moreover, the audit report shows that there is no causal relationship between the fact that Nanyang Shipping Company's books did not contain the land use right in question and the claim that Nanyang Real Estate Company enjoys the land use right in question. Therefore, the appellate argument of Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company that "according to the audit report and annual reports, as of the end of 2001, Nanyang Shipping Company's books did not include intangible assets such as land use rights, and therefore the land use right in question belongs to Nanyang Real Estate Company," also cannot be sustained.

In summary, the first-instance court's finding that Nanyang Real Estate Company does not enjoy the land use right in question is not improper. The reasons given by the appellants, Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company, that the first-instance court erred in finding that they do not enjoy the land use right in question, cannot be sustained.

II. Whether the RMB 2,000,000 loan between Chen Lin and Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company actually existed.

This Court holds that this case is a third-party revocation action, and Nanyang Real Estate Company is not a party to the aforementioned loan relationship. Whether that loan relationship actually existed is not within the scope of trial in this revocation action. However, acting in accordance with the principle of objectivity and fairness, the first-instance court also verified whether the RMB 2,000,000 loan between Chen Lin and Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company actually existed. Upon investigation, on May 15, 2002, Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company issued an IOU to Chen Lin, stating the facts of the loan relationship and the corresponding guarantee measures, and stamped with the "Financial Seal of Hainan Success Company" and the "Official Seal of Nanyang Shipping Company." Although the signature of "Fan Yunhai" was determined by forensic examination not to be his own, the act of Hainan Success Company affixing its "Financial Seal" on the IOU should be regarded as Hainan Success Company's acknowledgment of the validity of that IOU. Furthermore, the civil judgment of the Hubei High People's Court (2015) E-Min-Jian-San-Zai-Zhong Zi No. 00008, which has taken legal effect, determined that this IOU was genuine.

Nanyang Real Estate Company, Hainan Success Company, and Nanyang Shipping Company all argue that the RMB 2,000,000 loan is not genuine. Hainan Success Company claims it did not receive the RMB 2,000,000 loan. However, Chen Lin stated in court that at the time, because Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company were required by the regulatory authority to delist, their fund accounts were all frozen, and at the request of Fan Yunhai, the then chairman of the board of the original Hainan Success Company, the RMB 2,000,000 in cash was handed over to Fan Yunhai in three installments. Taken together with the relevant evidence submitted by Nanyang Real Estate Company, Hainan Success Company, and Nanyang Shipping Company, it can be confirmed that during the period of payment stated by Chen Lin, Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company were indeed undergoing asset restructuring. Moreover, Hainan Success Company and Nanyang Shipping Company did not provide any contrary evidence to rebut Chen Lin's statement, nor is it sufficient to prove that this case involved a situation of false litigation. Therefore, the first-instance court's finding that the RMB 2,000,000 loan was genuine is not improper.

As to the argument of Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company that Chen Lin's statements regarding the loan facts during the investigation by the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department were inconsistent, because that oral statement was not confirmed by the relevant judicial authority, and the Hainan Provincial Public Security Department did not, based on the said investigation, make a negative judgment on the existence of the loan or subsequently initiate criminal prosecution against Chen Lin, the first-instance court's failure to recognize the authenticity of the said oral statement is also not improper.

Regarding Hainan Success Company's appellate argument that Chen Lin had no objection to the authenticity of the eighth group of evidence, including his oral statement, upon examination, during the first-instance trial, Chen Lin's agent, Zhang Rongyou, acknowledged the authenticity of that group of evidence, but this does not constitute an acknowledgment of the content of the evidence. Therefore, this appellate argument cannot be sustained.

Viewed from the functional perspective of the third-party revocation action, its main purpose is to protect the rights and interests of third parties not participating in the original lawsuit who are harmed by erroneous effective judgments. At the same time, in judicial practice, abuse of this right of action, which would harm the stability of effective judgments, must also be prevented. Nanyang Real Estate Company claims that the content of the civil judgment of the Hubei High People's Court (2015) E-Min-Jian-San-Zai-Zhong Zi No. 00008 is erroneous and harms its civil rights and interests. It should provide evidence to prove that the result of that judgment is erroneous and that such error harms its civil rights and interests. The People's Court has already conducted multiple trials on whether the RMB 2,000,000 loan in question was genuine. The Hubei High People's Court, in its (2015) E-Min-Jian-San-Zai-Zhong Zi No. 00008 civil judgment, determined that the loan in question was genuine. Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company have not submitted evidence sufficient to overturn the original judgment. Therefore, this Court does not support their appellate argument that the RMB 2,000,000 loan in question is not genuine.

In summary, the appellate claims of Nanyang Real Estate Company and Hainan Success Company, lacking corresponding evidentiary support and legal basis, cannot be sustained and are hereby dismissed by this Court. The first-instance judgment is based on clear factual findings, correct application of law, and lawful trial procedures, and shall be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby orders as follows:

Appeal rejected, original judgment affirmed.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance shall be enforced in accordance with the first-instance judgment. The court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 23,680, to be borne equally by Hainan Nanyang Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Hainan Success Investment Co., Ltd., each paying RMB 11,840.

This judgment is final.
